title: Reduction of a CNF to a duplicate-free normal form
statement: Let $\psi$ be a CNF formula in the variables $x_1,\dots,x_n$, written as a conjunction of clauses, each clause a disjunction of literals. Then there is a CNF formula $\psi'$ that computes the same Boolean function as $\psi$, that is, $\psi'(x)=\psi(x)$ for every assignment $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, whose width (the maximum number of literals in any of its clauses) is at most that of $\psi$, and in which every clause is free of repetition in the strong sense that no literal occurs twice and no two distinct literals share a variable.
hypotheses_covered: input is an arbitrary CNF formula ψ in n variables
replaced:
For any CNF $\psi$ there exists a CNF $\psi'$ of width $\le$ that of $\psi$, evaluating
identically to $\psi$ on every input, with no duplicate literals in any clause and with
each clause variable-injective. Hence every CNF can be cleaned to satisfy the switching
lemma hypotheses.
